artifacts.summary: 5-phase plan applying the validated combined perf fix (single-pass jq @tsv extraction plus fork-free pure-bash term matching) behind a candidate-set equivalence gate.

memory_candidates.content: In bash hot loops, the dominant cost is usually fork/exec, not the tool being forked. Before optimizing an obvious 'N jq spawns per iteration' pattern, profile which helper is actually forking: shared helpers implemented as `echo "$x" | tr` or `echo "$h" | grep -qF "$n"` fork 2-6 processes per CALL and are invoked far more often than the per-iteration extraction. Replacing them with pure-bash `${var,,}` and `[[ "$h" == *"$n"* ]]` is typically a ~360x per-call win. Caveat to check when doing so: `${var,,}` is locale-aware and case-folds non-ASCII uppercase, while GNU `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'` operates bytewise and does not - so the pure-bash form can strictly ADD matches on a corpus with non-ASCII text. Also `$(echo "$1" | ...)` strips trailing newlines and swallows a bare `-n`/`-e` argument; `${1,,}` does neither. On a performance-only task these differences must be audited over the full corpus and surfaced, not silently accepted.
